threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a kebab shop instead of a 'kebab house'. The locals are quick to correct you after a late night out.
Caught a night bus last week, and there was a guy singing opera. Half the passengers were filming him, while the other half just pretended it wasn’t happening.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a group of kids setting up a makeshift cinema in the park with a projector and blankets, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you catch a U-Bahn strike and still grab some currywurst from a busker selling it out of a tent. Pure Berlin magic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can name all the taco trucks on Mission from 16th to 24th without missing a beat. Tourists just stick to the first one they see.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The other day, a guy serenaded the 38 with a ukulele and a heartbreaking rendition of 'Somewhere Over the Rainbow.' Feel like that sums up Muni perfectly.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the 'local' shops are all in Plaça del Sol; they miss the real gems hidden down Carrer de L'Encarnació, like that tiny bookstore.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their baffled expression while staring at the bus map in Gràcia, still expecting it to make sense.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still flinch every time the bus driver shouts ‘get on!’ instead of waiting for you to sit down. You’ll learn soon enough.
Caught a night bus to Brixton, and a guy in a parka serenaded the whole route with off-key Bohemian Rhapsody. The drivers just sighed, but we loved it.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy jogging with a beer in hand, weaving through families and street art. That’s the spirit of Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Kreuzberg's hidden U-Bahn stations have graffiti art that turns commuting into a mini gallery tour. It's like traveling through an urban museum daily.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows to carry dog biscuits after 5 pm to appease the pack of strays around Dolores Park. They’ll block your path otherwise.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo hopping on the 21 tonight, carrying a bouquet of flowers. Street style is peak San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals love 'festa major' noise, but many of us dread the late-night fireworks keeping our kids up.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they ask for 'tapas' instead of 'platos pequeños'—typically a dead giveaway in Gràcia.
